title: Noobie advice’s
author: Altruistic-Battle-38
selftext: Hi all, I and my friend wanna try to build 3d isometric online sandbox game. I’m using chat gpt and got some problems. For start I was using WORK SOL 6.1 hight for fun and it was great, he making a lot mechanics, I took free 3d assets. But then we decided to start from there, make strong server and etc, and started using chat GPT Codex 6.1 sol, it so slow, doing barely nothing as I can see for hourse. What difference? Is codex worst for coding then work, lol? And also maybe you have tips and tricks how to make it code faster and build an assets for my graphic?

comments.author: NoBatsHere
comments.body: No offense but if you're going to start this incredibly low effort you won't be able to get anything done. Go ask the AI for tips first. There's a lot you're doing wrong and it's obvious you aren't trying. If you come back with proof you've figured stuff out on your own and youre putting in real effort then people will help you more

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body:
I gotta chime in to what "NoBatsHere" said. He's right. That project that you're describing is incredibly ambitious. You have no knowledge of game design, no knowledge on how to even use AI properly to Code or develop a game. 

You should start with something much simpler and smaller, something that doesn't need an abundance of assets. You said you took free 3D Assets? Well congrats, you'll now forever be an Asset mash. You free assetss get you to 5% of your games visual, what happens to the other 95%? Ui? Enemies? Anything? You have to think much much further than you're doing right now. I wouldn't recommend working with SOL either. So my advice: Do a small game first to get some understanding of how to work with AI. Don't start with something ambitious like that.

I know you're probably really happy because SOL sharted something playable out in a few hours and you think you can build upon it. But trust me, i released a game before, you're in prototype stage, like 1% of your way to a full game. Prototypes are easy, its much harder to have a cohesive style and an enjoyable game.
